cause_quote: #86060 added `.option("--value-json", "Parse <value> as JSON for JSON/JSONC/JSONL leaf replacement")` and passed `{ valueJson: options.valueJson === true }` to setOcPath, but only the JSON branches read it, so YAML and Markdown targets accepted and ignored the flag.
user_saw: `openclaw path set ... --value-json` on a YAML or Markdown-frontmatter file reported success but wrote the JSON text as a plain string instead of a typed value.
summary: setOcPath now rejects valueJson for Markdown and YAML targets with a not-writable error that points to the plain positional value, leaving the file unchanged.
reasoning: The --value-json flag was introduced in 3a72a300 (#86060), after YAML support already existed (#81436), and from the start it was honored only for JSON/JSONC/JSONL while other formats silently dropped it, so the silent acceptance shipped with the flag. I read #86060's diff through the GitHub API; the exact non-JSON dispatch lines could not be read locally because the blob is missing, so confidence is medium.
